name: Herathian Voat
heading: Voat, Herathian
sourceWitness: Local TSR checked against the printed table and continuation text. pages count the cover.
habitatEvidence: The p. 116 table gives forest or plains. p. 117 describes seasonal movement between Herath, the Yazak Steppes, and western Hule.
appearanceEvidence: p. 117 describes the loose skin, oversized feet, blunt snout, no tail, and raking claws. The pale hide follows the reused portrait.
printingNotes: The print uses Slagovich juggernaut as an alias but also says a Slagovich juggernaut was created to hunt Herathian voats. Retain the printed encounter heading and the combat rules on these pages. No alternate stat block is inferred.

The appendix gives a brief War Cry save rule. The more detailed Campaign Book p. 107 distinguishes monsters with morale ratings from targets without them. The encounter summary uses the appendix version.

name: Jorri
heading: Jorri
sourceWitness: Local TSR checked against the printed table and continuation text. pages count the cover.
habitatEvidence: The table gives saltwater and p. 58 describes coastal dens, play in the surf, and reefs.
appearanceEvidence: pp. 57–58 describe short oily gray-black fur, white whiskers, webbed hind toes, and a crescent tail. These match the reused portrait.
printingNotes: Description gives 2–4 ft. length while the table gives 3–4 ft. The combat profile uses the table.
The source gives no extra attack bonus, recurring damage or fixed duration for the jaw lock.

name: Juhrion
heading: Juhrion
sourceWitness: Local TSR checked against the printed table and continuation text. pages count the cover.
habitatEvidence: The p. 58 table allows any terrain. p. 59 describes dens in caves or hollowed thicket beds.
appearanceEvidence: p. 58 explicitly describes the huge four-footed bear shape, lack of hair, red leathery hide, large teeth, and harpoon-shaped claws. The stance and muted shade are editorial.
printingNotes: Table lists special defenses as nil while ecology explicitly grants immunity to vermilia. The summary preserves both.

The claw paragraph gives a 50% infection chance and points to the Parasite entry, which gives the poison save. A practical reading is to roll the claw chance first and apply the appropriate save on exposure. The text does not state a roll order.

name: Lupasus
heading: Lupasus
sourceWitness: Local TSR checked against the printed table and continuation text. pages count the cover.
habitatEvidence: p. 68 gives any steppes and describes Yazak, prairies, forest lands, and all but the highest mountains.
appearanceEvidence: p. 68 describes a typical gray wolf shape with white underside, a bushy tail, and soft fur covering the wings. The reused portrait has layered wing edges.
printingNotes: The source lists no special attacks in its combat table. Flight rules and optional Legacy effects are described in prose.

name: Marine Cat
heading: Cat, Marine
sourceWitness: Local TSR checked against the printed table and continuation text. pages count the cover.
habitatEvidence: Table specifies shipboard and the prose describes dock outings and life around rigging, cargo holds, and staterooms.
appearanceEvidence: p. 16 describes a slightly larger-than-usual cat, often dark with bright eyes. The stripes and green eyes follow the reused portrait.
printingNotes: The glossary permits small family groups under Solitary. Retain the separate printed 1d2 number appearing.
The appendix gives no percentile chance or default Legacy, and neither named power belongs to an ordinary marine cat by default.
